assignments.node_id: מעצם גדלתו ורוממותו, שהוא מרומם מאד מדעתנו
assignments.reason: This node describes God's infinite greatness and exaltedness above human understanding. Its essential nature is divine transcendence — an attribute of holiness praising God's supreme elevation. It belongs with concepts about God's exalted nature and governance.

assignments.node_id: אי אפשר שנבין ונשיג בשכלנו הנהגתו יתברך
assignments.reason: This node states the impossibility of comprehending God's governance with human intellect. Its essential nature is the incomprehensibility of divine conduct — the other face of God's transcendence. It shares the same domain as God's exaltedness: both describe the reality that God's ways are beyond human grasp, which is portrayed in the teaching as fitting and beautiful for the Creator.

This node represents the existence of questions and difficulties about God. Its essential nature is the epistemic phenomenon of kushiyot — unanswerable questions that arise from the gap between human intellect and divine reality. The questions themselves are neither good nor evil; the teaching says they are necessary and fitting, a natural byproduct of God's transcendence. They belong in a separate domain from divine exaltedness itself.

new_packages.label: רוֹמְמוּת ה' וְהַנְהָגָתוֹ
new_packages.description: God's transcendent greatness and His governance beyond human comprehension. The teaching affirms that God's exaltedness above human understanding is fitting and beautiful — it would be improper if His ways conformed to our limited intellect.

new_packages.label: קֻשְׁיוֹת עַל ה'
new_packages.description: The inevitable questions and difficulties about God that arise because His ways transcend human understanding. The teaching frames these as necessary and fitting — not defects in faith but natural consequences of divine transcendence.
